business_problem: Capgemini needed a coding assistant that developers on regulated client projects would actually adopt, but public-cloud AI services conflicted with sovereignty rules and earlier open-source assistants were too inaccurate for daily use across modern and legacy codebases.
solution_summary: Capgemini built RAISE for Private Software Engineering, also known internally as SovBox, as a self-hosted software engineering assistant for regulated client work in aerospace, defense, and the public sector. The deployment kept existing IDE and CI/CD integrations in place while replacing the underlying model with Mistral's Codestral, so teams did not need to re-platform their development environments. Developers use the assistant for code completion and chatbot-style help across modern stacks and legacy languages such as ADA, C, and C++, with deployment methodology and coaching wrapped around the rollout to improve adoption. By keeping the service private and sovereignty-compliant, Capgemini could support projects that could not use public-cloud AI while still improving coding accuracy, workflow continuity, and delivery speed.

solution_components.name: RAISE for Private Software Engineering
solution_components.role: Provides Capgemini's internal private software engineering assistant for regulated client projects.

solution_components.name: Codestral
solution_components.role: Supplies the code-completion and chat model Capgemini runs inside the assistant.

data_flow: Developers invoke the private assistant from existing IDE and CI/CD workflows, the self-hosted platform routes coding and chat requests to Codestral, and the responses return inside the same tools without moving regulated client code into a public-cloud service.
integration_points: legacy application codebases in ADA, C, and C++
business_outcome: Capgemini raised developer adoption from 30 percent to 100 percent, improved code-completion accuracy from about 50 percent to 90 percent, and delivered productivity improvements across more than 50 client projects while meeting sovereignty requirements for regulated sectors.
metrics: 100% developer adoption rate across all client projects
90% code completion accuracy vs. 50% with previous solutions
50+ client projects reporting productivity improvements in less than 6 months
architecture_clues: The switch to Codestral required no changes to the existing infrastructure.
The assistant supports legacy languages including ADA, C, and C++ for applications dating back to the 1980s.
Capgemini says it is expanding to Codestral Embed and Devstral for RAG and CI/CD use cases.

"Developer adoption jumped from 30% to 100%, with all approximately 50 client projects reporting productivity savings."
